claim_formal.subject: Y Combinator portfolio companies
claim_formal.property: Number of portfolio companies that have achieved unicorn status ($1B+ valuation)
claim_formal.operator_note: 'Has backed' is interpreted cumulatively: any YC-funded company that has ever reached a $1B+ valuation, regardless of whether it remains privately valued at $1B+ today (some may have been acquired, gone public, or lost value). 'Unicorn' = startup valued at $1 billion or more. 'Since inception in 2005' = from the first YC batch (March 2005) through the present. Threshold: > 100 companies. Note: Counts vary by source and methodology — sources counting only currently private unicorns give lower numbers (Failory: 82 as of 2025) vs analyses counting all companies that have ever achieved unicorn status (Jared Heyman analysis of YC Top Companies list: 101 as of August 2022).

claim_natural: Y Combinator has backed over 100 unicorns since its inception in 2005.

B1.label: Jared Heyman / YC Top Companies list (Aug 2022): 101 YC unicorns

source.name: Jared Heyman (Medium): 'On 101 Y Combinator unicorns' — Analysis of YC's official Top Companies list (August 2022)
source.quote: In August 2022, Y Combinator released its latest Top Companies list, now including 314 private and 16 public YC startups each valued at over $150M. The 101 YC unicorns account for nearly 90% of all Top Companies' value

credibility.note: Unclassified domain — verify source authority manually

B2.label: PitchBook: YC leads accelerators in unicorn creation (5.8% of 2010-2015 cohorts)

source.name: PitchBook: Y Combinator leads among accelerators in unicorn-creation rate
source.quote: Around 5.8 percent of startups in Y Combinator's 2010 to 2015 cohorts have become unicorns, which means they're valued at over $1 billion

credibility.note: Unclassified domain — verify source authority manually

adversarial_checks.verification_performed: Failory.com publishes 'The Full List of 82 Unicorn Startups Backed by Y Combinator' as of 2025. This count is lower than 101 because it tracks only currently private companies valued at $1B+. Companies that went public (e.g., Airbnb, DoorDash, Coinbase, Reddit, Stripe via IPO), were acquired at unicorn valuations, or had their valuations marked down are excluded from this count. The claim's 'has backed' language encompasses all-time unicorns, making 101 (all-time) the appropriate comparator. The 82 active count does not contradict a cumulative count of >100.

adversarial_checks.description: YC's own 'Top Companies' list is self-reported
adversarial_checks.verification_performed: YC's Top Companies list is curated by YC itself and relies on self-reported or publicly disclosed valuations. For private companies, valuations are typically from their last funding round. YC has incentive to maximize the perceived value of its portfolio. However, PitchBook (an independent data provider) confirms YC's unicorn creation rate as the highest among all accelerators, corroborating the order of magnitude of the claim.

adversarial_checks.description: Valuations fluctuate — some unicorns may have lost that status
adversarial_checks.verification_performed: In 2022-2023, many private tech company valuations were marked down by 30-70%. Some YC companies that reached $1B+ valuations at peak (2021) may have been repriced below $1B. However, the claim uses present perfect ('has backed'), which covers historical unicorn achievement, not current valuations. Companies that were once valued at $1B+ but fell below still count under the cumulative interpretation.
